main_text.p: שׁוּד Linere, Oblinere: Præterit. וַיִּשְׁדֹּ[?] אוֹתָם בַּשִּׂיד[?] Et oblines eos calce, Deut.27.4.
שִׂיד[?] m. Calx, ut in præced. loco, & Amos 2.1.

שׁוּהַ Æquari, Adæquari, Æqualem esse: Utile esse, Prodesse, Convenire, Expedire. Construitur cum Præpositione ב & ל. Præterit. לֹא שׁוּה לִי[?] וְלִפְלֹךְ אֵין שׁוּה[?] Et non profuerat mihi, Job.33.27. Partic. פָּוֹחְתִשְׁוּה לוֹ[?] Et regi non est utile, Esth.3.8. Futur. לֹא־תִשְׁוֶה[?] Ne adæquëris ei, Proverb.26.4. לֹא יִשְׁוּ בָהּ[?] Non possunt æquari ei, Proverb.3.15. Niph. vide in Hithpahel. Pih. שִׁוָּה[?] Æquavit, Poluit, Compositum, Disposuit, Propo-suit, ex significatione Chaldaica: Præter. שִׁוִּיתִי Proponebam, Jesa.38.13. Partic. מְשַׁוֶּה רַגְלַי Disponens pedes meos, 2.Sam.22.34. Chald. Præterit. עִם־הַחַיָּא שַׁוִּי[?] Cum bestiis posuit, ad bestias applicuit, Daniel.5.21. Hiph. Futur. מַה־אַשְׁוֶה־לָּךְ Quid æquabo tibi, Thren.2.13. וְתֻשְׁוּ[?] Et æquabitis, Jesa.46.5. Hithp. נִשְׁתַּוָּה[?] Æquatur, Prov.27.15. forma composita ex Niphal & Hithpahel: Simile in כַּפֵּר[?]. Chald. Fut. וּבֵיתֵהּ נְוֵלִי יִשְׁתַּוֵּה[?] Et domus ejus sterquilinium ponatur, Dan.3.29.

שׁוּחַ Inclinari, Propendere: Præteriit. Fœminin. כִּי שׁחָה אֶל מָוֶת בֵּיתָהּ[?] Nam propendet ad mortem domus ejus, Proverb.2.18. R.Joseph à שׁחה[?] deduxit, pro Deprimitur, Incurvat se, Inclinat ad mortem domus ejus, sensu eodem, nihil obstante quòd sit penacutum. Atque sic manet conveniëntia generis inter Verbum, & Nomen בִּין[?], quod semper masculinum est: si verò sit à שׁוח, tunc est fœmininum, & genere discrepat à masculino בִּין[?].
שׁוּחָה f. Fossa, Fovea, Jer.18.20. שׁוּחָה עָמֻקָּה Fossa profunda, Prov.22.14. וְשׁוּחָה Et fovea, Jer.2.6.
שִׂיחָה f. Idem, Psal.57.7. Plural. שִׂיחוֹת Psal.119.85.

page.notes: Hebrew vocalisation and several consonantal readings are faint or partly obscured by print and scan blur; they are copied as best read and marked [?]. The printed words are in the reading order of the page. The bottom right catchword is printed alone below the last full line. Latin text is transcribed as printed, including "penacutum", "Poluit", "Jesa" and "Compositum", which are printing forms and were left unchanged. The entry headwords are set in Hebrew type and copied as printed; they are not marked as headings because they are dictionary entries within running text.
